metadata.methods_description: EEG was recorded with an ANT Neuro system (64 channels, 1000 Hz sampling rate) while participants performed dribble (5 conditions), ballpass (4 conditions), and two-person passing tasks (4 combined conditions and 4 PLV conditions). Raw data, preprocessed data, and PLV functional connectivity results are provided.

citation_details.title: Dataset for Multiple Basketball Motor Observation and Motor Imagery Based on Functional Connectivity Analysis
citation_details.author: Jiaqi Wang, Ming Tang, Lingrong Jia, Jinxiang Zhang, Cheng Cheng, Jiahui Han
citation_details.abstract: This study presents an electroencephalography (EEG) dataset collected during motor imagery (MI) and motor observation (MO) of basketball-specific actions, designed to support functional connectivity research and facilitate brain-computer interface (BCI) development. Thirty-five healthy right-handed participants completed three experimental protocols: single-hand dribbling, bilateral ball tapping (throwing the ball from one hand to the other), and two-person passing. The three protocols included different types of MI and MO tasks, yielding 1,560 trials per participant with a total recording duration of approximately 70 min. The dataset provides raw recordings, preprocessed data, and functional connectivity matrices based on phase-locking values (PLV) across multiple frequency bands and time windows. Additional metadata included demographic information and scores from the KVIQ-20, which assesses motor-imagery ability. This dataset enables investigations into the neural mechanisms underlying MI and MO in ecologically valid sports contexts and the evaluation of functional connectivity metrics and may even offer opportunities for the development of functional connectivity-based MI-BCI applications.
